claims.text: Controlled potential pre-conditioning induces reversible surface oxidation and reduction on platinum-group metal nanoparticles.
Pre-conditioning produces an optimally thin oxide/hydroxide surface layer.
The oxide/hydroxide layer optimizes the binding dynamics of ethanol-oxidation intermediates.
Optimized intermediate binding enhances electron-transfer processes during ethanol oxidation.
Optimized intermediate binding enhances proton-transfer processes during ethanol oxidation.
Reversible oxide/hydroxide modulation improves catalytic activity.
Reversible oxide/hydroxide modulation improves catalytic selectivity.
Reversible oxide/hydroxide modulation improves catalytic durability.
The initial supported platinum-group metal nanoparticles have predominantly metallic surfaces.
Balanced oxidation-state modulation changes the adsorption and desorption kinetics of ethanol-oxidation intermediates.
Balanced reversible oxidation-state modulation avoids irreversible catalyst degradation.
Complete ethanol oxidation proceeds through a 12-electron, 12-proton pathway.
Pre-conditioned catalysts will exhibit lower overpotentials than untreated catalysts.
Pre-conditioned catalysts will exhibit higher current densities than untreated catalysts.
Pre-conditioned catalysts will exhibit greater durability than untreated catalysts.
The proposed mechanism applies to alkaline ethanol oxidation at approximately 60 °C.
Excessively high potentials or temperatures can cause irreversible surface oxidation and invalidate the proposed reversible mechanism.
Acidic reaction conditions can have interfacial chemistry different from alkaline conditions, so the proposed mechanism may not apply.
